les: Wat 'n dier in sy habitat kry
kaps_punt: diere moet 'n habitat hê vir kos, water, 'n plek om te skuiling, babas te hê en om veilig te wees

items.bewering: 'n Dier moet 'n habitat hê om aan die lewe te bly. Die plek waar hy lewe, gee hom die dinge wat hy nodig het.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Habitat' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/habitat/): 'A habitat is a place where an organism makes its home'; a habitat has to supply food, water, shelter and space to raise young.

items.bewering: 'n Sebra vreet die lang gras wat in die grasveld groei. Die grasveld self bied dus die kos wat hierdie dier nodig het.
items.blok: Kos en water in die habitat
items.bron: Mpala Research Centre field guide, plains zebra (mpala.org/field_guide/view/plains_zebra/): grass is more than 90% of the diet, the zebra lives in grassland and grassland with scattered bush, and it eats the fibrous stems other grazers leave. Bell (1971, Scientific American) and later secondary accounts: in the grazing succession zebras crop the tallest, coarsest grass first. Nuance, which does not make the claim false: Mpala says plains zebras PREFER short new growth when they can get it. The lesson says the zebra eats tall grass, not that it prefers it, and that is true.

items.bewering: Dieselfde grasveld bied ook water in 'n watergat waaruit hy kan drink.
items.blok: Kos en water in die habitat
items.bron: Mpala field guide, plains zebra: it needs a constant water source and rarely moves more than about 12 km from one. Other zoo fact sheets say it drinks every day.

items.bewering: In die grasveld kruip 'n vlakvark weg in 'n gat in die grond. Die gat hou die reën weg en verberg hom.
items.bron: San Diego Zoo warthog fact sheet (ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/warthog_common/behavior): burrows give shelter from cold or rain at night, from daytime heat and from predators. SANParks, common warthog (sanparks.org, Marakele): they shelter in large holes, usually old aardvark burrows. Kruger Park guide: they back into the hole tail first.

items.bewering: So 'n gat is een plek binne die habitat en nie die habitat self nie.
items.bron: SANParks, common warthog: a warthog may use one hole for a few nights in a row, but it does not use any one hole for long. It forages across the grassland and savanna, so the hole is a shelter inside its habitat and not the habitat itself. National Geographic Education counts shelter as one PART of a habitat.

items.bewering: 'n Skoolveld kan ook 'n habitat wees, want gras lewe daar. 'n Gat daarin is een plek binne daardie habitat.
items.bron: True under the lesson's own definition and the dictionary one. Vocabulary.com / Wordnik (American Heritage) define a habitat as the natural environment where a species, plant or animal, lives, so a field where grass grows is the grass's habitat. Mapping check: the reason given ('because grass lives there') is a sufficient reason, not the only one. A learner who reasons 'no grass, so no habitat' would go wrong, but the sentence does not say that. No correction needed.

items.bewering: Baie paddas lê hulle eiers in die stil water van 'n rivier. Daardie stil water gee die kleintjies 'n plek om groot te word.
items.bron: South African species accounts. Biodiversity Database of Iziko (thebdi.org), raucous toad: breeds at farm dams, ponds and pools along slow-flowing streams, and lays egg strings among water plants. Wikipedia (FrogMAP-based), Cape river frog: prefers deep, still water for breeding, where its tadpoles grow. SAHRA fauna appendix: painted reed frog in slow rivers, and other species in still reaches of rivers. So 'many frogs' using the quiet water of a river holds. Note for the writer, not a fault: across South Africa most still-water breeders use ponds, dams, vleis and pans more often than rivers. The sentence is narrow but true.

items.bewering: 'n Habitat gee 'n dier ook maniere om weg te kom van wat hom jag. In die oop grasveld sien 'n sebra 'n leeu van ver af aankom. Dan kan hy wegkom voordat die leeu naby genoeg kom.
items.bron: Hopcraft, Sinclair & Packer 2005, J. Anim. Ecol. (esf.edu PDF): lions are stalk-and-ambush hunters that depend on good cover, and they feed where prey is catchable rather than where it is plentiful. Chen et al. 2025, Ecol. Evol. (PMC12077961) cites earlier work: zebras flee from bushy areas and choose open grassland when they run. Mapping check: the sentence says 'kan', a possibility, and does not claim that open ground always saves the zebra, so it holds. Lions also hunt at night, when seeing far does not help, but the sentence does not deny that.

items.bewering: habitat: Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: Read on its own as well as in its block. Wordnik (American Heritage): 'the natural environment in which a species or group of species lives'. National Geographic Education: 'a place where an organism makes its home'. The definition is simple and true, and it covers plants, which the schoolfield sentence relies on.

opsomming: Elke kontroleerbare bewering is bevestig, en die les het geen oortreffende trappe of vergelykings nie. Twee nuanses breek niks nie: sebras eet lang gras, maar verkies vars kort gras as hulle dit kan kry; en die meeste paddas lê hulle eiers eerder in damme en vleie as in 'n rivier se stil water.
